rendered: The anode-free full cell, built with a presodiated pyrite cathode, reaches an energy density of ∼400 Wh/kg[1]. This is calculated from the mass of the presodiated pyrite and the carbon nucleation layer, assuming a Na1.5FeS2 stoichiometry ("calculated based on the mass of" the presodiated pyrite, p5.L51-L53). The paper gives the theoretical maximum for LIB technology as 387 Wh/kg for LiCoO2/graphite cells[2]. So the cell's value is slightly above that LiCoO2/graphite ceiling. The paper qualifies the LIB comparison: the cell exceeds all previous SIB reports, and, assuming a 50%[3] packaging penalty, exceeds current LIB technology[4]. In other words, the claim of beating LIB technology depends on that packaging assumption.
